agents.name: Bob
memories: Water is the constraint that ends farms.
Do not plant more than we can water.

today.why: Harvest is in the bin and a new row just went in. Water is the constraint that ends farms — clear sky still pulls three points a day even with the ditch, and I will not let a fresh sprout start thirsty.
today.expect: East field moisture held high so the sprout can push toward growing without a dry dip.

yesterday.why: The stalks are ripe now. Leaving ripe corn on the stalk is how a careful farm turns into a hungry one — get it in the bin before weather or pests write a different ending.
yesterday.expect: Corn in storage, field clear, food buffer thick enough for the next stretch.

agents.name: Alice
memories: Unused seeds are a delay, not a reserve.
Ditches compound. Heat does not wait.

today.why: Bob will spend cistern on the new row. Ditches compound only if the tank stays fat — heat does not wait, and topping up now beats scrambling when the gauge drops.
today.expect: Cistern refilled after irrigation so the next dry stretch never touches zero.

yesterday.why: Unused seeds are a delay, not a reserve. The moment the row clears, put the next one in — heat does not wait for a tidy schedule.
yesterday.expect: A seeded row again so we do not sit on an empty field while the cistern and ditch already work.
